newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU commissioner pledges careful review before EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU commissioner pledges careful review before EMU.

text.p: The European Commission will carefully evaluate nations' economic credentials to ensure they lay the groundwork for lasting stability for Europe's planned currency union, a senior EU official said on Wednesday.

In an interview with the Handelsblatt business daily European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said it was important nations meet all the entry criteria for the currency union and prove their data is not just a one-off success.

He said a nation would not automatically qualify to join the union, at its scheduled launch on January 1, 1999, even if it met the three percent budget defict reference point in 1997, one of the criteria laid down in the Maastricht Treaty.

De Silguy said the Commission and the European Monetary Institute will judge nations' progress to see whether sufficient convergence has been achieved and for this the evaluation of one year's economic data would not be sufficient.
"In our report to the leaders of government we will strictly apply the Treaty's criteria and show that the convergence will be high and durable," the paper quoted de Silguy as saying.
De Silguy also said current projections that a large number of nations would qualify to join the first group of nations in the currency union should not be misinterpreted as fact.
These projections were based on budget plans, de Silguy said, warning that the actual numbers may be quite different when reviewed in 1998.
At the same time de Silguy said nations were making some steps towards adopting the new currency union.
De Silguy welcomed the so-called stability pact, the brain-child of German finance minister Theo Waigel, designed to ensure lasting fiscal discipline after monetary union.
He was also optimistic that ongoing negotiations about the issue would result in an acceptable compromise before the meeting of EU economics and finance ministers in Dublin on December 13.
